metadata.title: R Code Supporting "Dietary and Lifestyle Correlates of Gut Microbiota Diversity and Composition in Healthy Adults: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study Informing Longitudinal Research"
metadata.description:
This repository contains the R code supporting the study “Dietary and Lifestyle Correlates of Gut Microbiota Diversity and Composition in Healthy Adults: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study Informing Longitudinal Research.”

The code implements the downstream analytical workflow used to examine associations between four continuous dietary and lifestyle exposures—Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS) score, ultra-processed-food consumption score, International Physical Activity Questionnaire–Short Form (IPAQ-SF) MET-min/week, and an adapted sleep score—and genus-level gut microbiota outcomes in 20 healthy adults.

The workflow includes data validation; descriptive microbiome analyses; Shannon diversity and Pielou’s evenness models; Bray–Curtis and Aitchison beta-diversity analyses; age- and sex-adjusted PERMANOVA; centered log-ratio analyses of eight prespecified bacterial genera; analysis of the natural-log-transformed Prevotella/Bacteroides ratio; false-discovery-rate correction; model diagnostics; influence and sensitivity analyses; scenario-based sample-size calculations; and generation of the data-driven main and supplementary figures.

The archive contains ten numbered analytical and visualization scripts, a shared R functions file, a complete workflow runner, and a numerical validation script. It does not contain participant-level data, questionnaires, analytical results, tables, or figures.

Raw 16S rRNA gene sequencing data are available through the European Nucleotide Archive under study accession PRJEB107991.

hits.title: R Code Supporting "Dietary and Lifestyle Correlates of Gut Microbiota Diversity and Composition in Healthy Adults: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study Informing Longitudinal Research"

metadata.title: Numerical codes for simulating **one and two-dimensional porosity waves and focused fluid migration in deformable porous media
metadata.description:
This package contains numerical codes for simulating **one and two-dimensional porosity waves and focused fluid migration in deformable porous media**, including viscoelastic compaction, porosity advection, and solid-matrix advection.
The repository contains both **1D Python and 2D Julia implementations** of the numerical model and is intended to support reproducibility of the simulations presented in the associated publication titled "Effects of Viscoelastic Compaction and Advection on Porosity Wave Propagation in the Subsurface"

## Overview

Porosity waves provide a mechanism for localized and potentially rapid fluid migration through deformable porous media. This model investigates how **viscoelastic compaction**, together with fluid and solid advection, influences the initiation, propagation, and morphology of porosity-wave-driven fluid channels.

The model couples the following physical processes:
* Stokes flow of the solid matrix
* Darcy flow of the fluid phase
* Viscoelastic compaction of the porous matrix
* Porosity advection through solid-matrix advection
* Porosity-dependent permeability
* Coupled evolution of fluid pressure, solid pressure, and porosity

The viscoelastic rheology allows both **elastic compaction** and **viscous compaction** to contribute to the evolution of the coupled solid–fluid system.

journal.title: Effects of Viscoelastic Compaction and Advection on Porosity Wave Propagation in the Subsurface

metadata.title: CROC Core v6 Reproducibility Package: A Novel Cancellation-Resolution Ownership Consistency Algorithm for Asynchronous WebAssembly Components
metadata.description:
This record provides the final Core v6 reproducibility package for the study:

“CROC: A Novel Cancellation-Resolution Ownership Consistency Algorithm for Asynchronous WebAssembly Components.”

CROC is a trace-based decision algorithm for checking cancellation-resolution ownership consistency in asynchronous WebAssembly component executions. The final Core v6 formulation tracks task lifecycle state, cancellation requests, resource ownership, explicit borrowed-handle identities and multiplicity, and resolution-specific obligations for returned, cancelled-before-started, and cancelled-before-returned outcomes.

This package freezes the executable Core v6 implementation used by the final manuscript together with the validation scripts, experiment artifacts, raw performance measurements, manifests, and formal correctness material.

Final validation evidence included in this release comprises:

• Exact Core v5/Core v6 historical equivalence on 4,300/4,300 cases.

• Independent bounded exhaustive validation with complete agreement on:
  – 3,180/3,180 legal prefixes;
  – 17,937/17,937 bounded one-step decisions;
  – 9,540/9,540 resolution decisions;
  – 5,336/5,336 independently determined resolution diagnostic checks; and
  – 954/954 multi-borrow resolution cases.

• Core v6 performance evaluation across 18 configurations and 720 measured repetitions, including raw timing samples, dispersion statistics, bootstrap confidence intervals, Python allocation measurements, and fresh-process Windows RSS measurements.

• Scalability evaluation up to 10,000 tasks. The 10,000-task clean configuration completed in a median of 15.063 ms with a p95 of 15.535 ms, while the late-cancellation configuration completed in a median of 18.173 ms with a p95 of 18.768 ms.

• Borrow-width evaluation up to 1,024 explicit borrowed handles.

• A formal correctness package containing the prefix-state invariant, resolution characterization, borrow-multiplicity preservation proposition, decision-correctness theorem, first-witness minimality theorem, and deterministic diagnostic-selection corollary.

The independent bounded exhaustive validation is exhaustive over its explicitly defined finite model. The formal correctness results are stated relative to the normalized CROC event semantics implemented by the frozen Core v6.

Reproducibility package ZIP SHA-256:

metadata.title: IgG1 Analysis Tools: AlphaFold Y-Shape Studio for screening AlphaFold 3 antibody models
metadata.description:
AlphaFold Y-Shape Studio 1.3.0 is a desktop application for screening AlphaFold 3 IgG1 antibody models and inspecting their structures with Matplotlib. It assigns chains and domains, measures hinge and Fab/Fc geometry, reports candidate disulfide bonds, and provides an interactive three-dimensional preview. Analysis runs locally.

Changes in version 1.3.0

  • Matplotlib/Tk is the only viewer; OpenGL code and dependencies have been removed.
  • Revised interface with light and dark themes, progress, cancellation, stable model selection, keyboard controls, camera reset, and PNG/SVG/PDF export.
  • Corrected Fc descriptors to use a molecule-relative axis, making them invariant to rigid rotation. Thresholds are unchanged; Fc values can differ from version 1.2.0.
  • Separate output folders for each completed run, preserved previous results.
  • Corrected Linux environment selection and a Windows executable built from the same versioned source.

Downloads

  • Windows: AlphaFold_Y_Shape_Studio_Windows_x86_64_v1.3.0.zip contains the ready-to-run executable and its bundled runtime. Extract the entire ZIP and keep the _internal folder beside the executable. Python installation is not required. The executable is unsigned; do not disable operating-system security protections.
  • Linux and source: AlphaFold_Y_Shape_Studio_Source_v1.3.0.tar.gz contains the source, pinned requirements, installer/launchers, regression tests, and build instructions. The tested configuration uses Python 3.10 with Tk and venv. Run bash install_and_run.sh from the extracted folder; the first installation requires internet access.
  • Both archives include the complete 15-model sample dataset, documentation, dependency notices, and the upstream MDAnalysis source archive.

Validation and limitations

Software testing covers Windows 11 x64 and Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2/WSLg, including 75 regression tests on each platform, the bundled Windows executable, geometric invariance, malformed inputs, output preservation, profile comparisons, and interface/export behaviour. The supplied IgG1 sample produces 15 analyzed structures, 3 passing models. See README.md for tested configurations and limitations.

This software is a geometric screening tool for AlphaFold3 output, not experimental validation of structure, function, or biological activity.

metadata.title: Structural Covariance Network Analysis in EPM1: An R-Based Graph-Theoretical and Permutation Testing Pipeline
metadata.description:
This software provides a reproducible R workflow for whole-brain structural covariance network (SCN) analysis in progressive myoclonus epilepsy type 1 (EPM1; Unverricht–Lundborg disease) and healthy controls. Regional brain volumes are normalized to total intracranial volume and residualized for age and sex. Group-level weighted structural covariance networks are then constructed from Pearson correlations between regional measures, retaining positive correlations at a fixed threshold of r ≥ 0.30.

The pipeline calculates global network density, global efficiency, transitivity, modularity, average path length, and nodal efficiency. Group differences are evaluated using 5,000 label permutations, with false discovery rate correction applied to nodal comparisons. The script also exports the patient-minus-control edge-difference matrix and derives leave-one-out (jackknife) subject contribution measures for global network metrics and a predefined nodal metric, enabling subsequent association analyses with clinical variables.

The workflow uses interactive input-file and output-directory selection and therefore contains no hard-coded data paths. Participant-level imaging and clinical data are not included.

Keywords: EPM1; Unverricht–Lundborg disease; progressive myoclonus epilepsy; structural covariance network; structural MRI; graph theory; network neuroscience; nodal efficiency; permutation testing; R.

metadata.title: Reproducibility package for "Multi-timescale PTM architecture in human RNA polymerase II"
metadata.description: Human RNA polymerase II (Pol II) carries an extensive landscape of post-translational modifications (PTMs) and conformational states that collectively coordinate transcription and co-transcriptional RNA processing. Here, we compile residue-level annotations across the twelve human Pol II subunits and formulate an explicit discrete-state framework for the C-terminal domain, the non-CTD region of Rpb1, and subunits Rpb2–Rpb12. Under an independent-site construction, the curated residue-state landscape has a maximum logarithmic state-space size of 707.98 bits per Pol II molecule, including 211.22 bits contributed by the CTD. Experimental human CTD mass-spectrometry data support the five canonical phosphoacceptor-position classes represented in the framework and show qualitative agreement between the predominant Ser5-P and Ser2-P classes and the largest modeled position-class contributions. Empirical kinetic observations further support a multi-timescale architecture spanning seconds to hours. The quantitative framework distinguishes model-defined state-space size from physiological entropy and provides a reproducible approach to PTM-rich regulatory systems.
metadata.notes: If you use this reproducibility package, please cite both the archived software/data package and the associated manuscript.

metadata.title: topology-fingerprints: empirical tests for a topological framework of claims and resources
metadata.description:
Empirical arm of a topological framework in which a monetary claim and the resource it points at are distinct objects. The companion repository builds the mechanism models; this one goes looking for those mechanisms in published national accounts and statistical tables. Nothing here is simulated and nothing is fitted to a target.

Across 18 countries and 881 country-years, in years when broad money grows 10 percentage points faster than nominal GDP, nominal house prices rise about 2.3 percentage points faster than nominal wages (gamma = 0.2319, country-block bootstrap p = 0.002), which reads directly against monetary neutrality. Controlling for the Schularick-Taylor credit benchmark, the five-year cumulative form of the same wedge lifts crisis-prediction AUC from 0.677 to 0.705 across 17 countries and 150 years, with the functional form selected by the data. On its own the wedge reaches 0.676 against that benchmark's 0.677.

A third line measured the resolution ceiling of the instruments available to it: at horizon h of about 50, seventeen countries stacked together supply 5.3 independent windows, and that number bounds every future claim made on this data.

RESULTS.md carries every station with its verdict, and its section 2 carries the citation limits. Code is MIT; documentation and results are CC BY 4.0.

metadata.title: TheDongLab/AI2AMP-PD: AI2AMP-PD v1.0
metadata.description:
This is the first public release of the analysis code accompanying the manuscript "Differential expression and machine-learning classification of Parkinson's disease using AMP-PD RNA-seq data" (Hu R, Dong X, et al.).

Overview

Analysis pipeline for RNA-seq–based differential expression (DE) and machine-learning (ML) classification of Parkinson's disease (PD) case/control status, using AMP-PD cohorts PPMI and PDBP/BioFIND (PDBF).

What's included

  • Data preparation — build case/control and mutation-carrier sample sets and extract per-cohort RNA-seq quantification matrices (DE/src/filtration.py, DE/src/extract_quant.py)
  • Differential expression — DESeq2-based DE analysis for genes, eRNAs, and circRNAs, adjusted for covariates (age, sex, plate, RIN, genotype PCs) (DE/src/DE_PCs.R, DE/src/eRNA/, DE/src/circRNA/)
  • Functional enrichment — GO/KEGG/Reactome/GSEA analysis on DE results (DE/src/Enrich_Profiler.R)
  • ML classification — logistic regression, LASSO, SVM, random forest, XGBoost, KNN, MLP, and stepwise feature-addition classifiers trained on PPMI and independently tested on PDBF (ML/src/*.py)
  • Model evaluation — combined AUROC/PR curve and feature-importance summary plots (ML/src/31_plots_AUC_PR_inOne.py)
  • NanoString QC — standalone endogenous/housekeeping gene QC script (DE/NanoStringData/)
  • Recorded R/Python session info and pinned dependencies (session_info/)

Requirements

  • R ≥ 4.0 (tidyverse, DESeq2, clusterProfiler, and related Bioconductor/CRAN packages)
  • Python ≥ 3.8 (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn)

Known limitations

  • Scripts are tailored to the specific AMP-PD sample sets and covariate schemas used in this study; not general-purpose tools
  • File paths and cohort-specific parameters are set via literals/CLI args and may need editing for new datasets
  • Raw AMP-PD data are not distributed with this repository; access requires a separate application to the AMP-PD Knowledge Portal (https://amp-pd.org/)

License

MIT License

metadata.title: QQA4CO: Quasi-Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization
metadata.description:
QQA 0.9.0 — Typed primal-dual runtime

QQA 0.9.0 promotes QQA4CO from a primal-search toolkit to a typed, auditable primal-dual and hybrid optimisation runtime while preserving the existing research APIs.

Highlights

  • Stable solve, plan, and inspect contracts backed by machine-readable model/factor capabilities, strict finite bounds, and tri-state feasibility.
  • Robust normalized QQA dynamics, heterogeneous replicas, tempering exchange, factor preconditioning, historical archives, adaptive augmented Lagrangians, and archive-centred restarts.
  • Device-resident typed factor operations, GPU repair/local search, bounded autotuning, and roofline telemetry.
  • Sparse PDHG, dual crossover, SCIP feedback, general QUBO persistency, isolated exact workers, CP-SAT scheduling, and SAT/MaxSAT runtimes.
  • Benders, column generation, progressive hedging, spatial branch-and-bound, DRO/scenario/SAA tools, black-box acquisition, and OOD-gated learned planning.
  • Pickle-free atomic checkpoints, checksum-protected result packages, bounded schema-only service jobs, Model Doctor, Optimization Cockpit, Decision Explorer, and domain templates.
  • Refreshed documentation and a credential-free typed primal-dual notebook covering diagnosis, events, visualization, resume, and package verification.

Validation

  • CI passed on CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
  • The built-in correctness sweep passed 29/29 checks, including exact -N energies for periodic ferromagnetic Ising instances through N=64.
  • Secret scan, strict documentation build/deploy, full-source type checking, package build, Twine metadata checks, archive portability scans, and the performance gate passed.

See the 0.9.0 changelog and next-generation runtime guide for details.

metadata.description:
This repository contains the reproducibility code associated with the manuscript “Explainable AI-Driven Multi-Horizon ROP Forecasting for Risk-Aware Drilling Decision Support.”

The archive includes the data preprocessing pipeline, baseline implementations, RMC-Transformer training code, repeated-run experiments, statistical analysis, risk-parameter sensitivity analysis, and the external validation workflow on the public Volve/USROP benchmark.

The public USROP dataset used for external validation is available at:
https://github.com/AndrzejTunkiel/USROP
and is described in:
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.petrol.2020.108069
The original Volve field data are available from Equinor at:
https://www.equinor.com/energy/volve-data-sharing

The Oman-6ROP dataset is not included in this repository. It is derived from proprietary industrial drilling data and cannot be publicly redistributed because of intellectual-property ownership, confidentiality, privacy, contractual, and data-use restrictions. Access, if considered, remains subject to permission from the industrial data owner and the applicable confidentiality and data-use agreements.

The repository therefore provides the complete software workflow and configuration files, while the restricted Oman industrial data must be supplied separately by authorized users.
